subject: Evaluation: catalog listing vs enterprise purchase — timeline & legal implications
messages:
From: Julia Singh <julia.singh@acme.software>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, Apr 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Marketplace vs direct purchase — procurement questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to do a quick comparison so they can decide whether to buy Redwood via our cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) or by executing a direct contract (PO + master services agreement). They want the pros/cons in terms of:

- Procurement timeline (how quickly can we be transactable/paid)
- Invoicing & payment terms (PO vs marketplace invoice; monthly invoicing vs SaaS billing)
- Discounts and commercial flexibility (can we get enterprise pricing vs marketplace price?)
- Entitlements & seat/license management (how are seats/entitlements tracked for marketplace subscriptions?)
- Co-sell / incentives (if we buy via cloud marketplace, will that enable co-sell incentives from cloud provider?)
- Compliance evidence (SOC 2, data residency, audit support — any difference by route?)
- Termination / data portability (e.g., export of logs/kv-cache if we stop service)

Can you provide a short write-up or call with procurement next week? I attached their initial questionnaire.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Singh
IT Sourcing Lead — Acme Software
Procurement | acme.software

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Marketplace vs direct purchase — procurement questions

Hi Julia — great to hear the demo landed well. High-level answer below; I can join procurement next Tue/Wed for a 30-min sync and bring our channel lead. I attached a short one-pager that summarizes the tradeoffs.

High-level comparison (marketplace vs direct):

1) Procurement timeline
- Marketplace: usually fastest to transact for standard SaaS listings (hours–days) once the listing is published and terms accepted by buyer. Private offers (Azure/GCP private offers, AWS Marketplace private offers) can take a few days to a couple weeks if a custom billing arrangement is needed.
- Direct contract: typically slower — legal review + PO issuance often 2–6 weeks for mid-market customers, longer for enterprise.

2) Invoicing & payment terms
- Marketplace: buyer is billed through the cloud provider; provider issues invoice and collects payment. That can simplify PO reconciliation (you still accept provider invoice) but marketplaces may have limited custom payment terms (net30 is common but negotiated terms are rarer).
- Direct: Redwood invoices Acme directly; flexible payment terms and special invoicing flows (annual prepay, multi-year SOWs) are easier to support.

3) Commercial flexibility & discounts
- Marketplace: list price tends to be public; private offers or marketplace transactions with negotiated discounts are possible but require provider commerce flow (private offers) and sometimes have programmatic constraints. Marketplace fees (percent fee to the cloud vendor) reduce our margin which affects discounting.
- Direct: enables bespoke discounts, true enterprise pricing, and bundling (e.g., Dedicated/Private deployments + support).

4) Entitlements & seat management
- Marketplace: entitlements are typically managed via the cloud provider’s subscription system (license linking or marketplace contract). This can complicate seat transfers across accounts, but we support linking customer identity and SSO to map entitlements.
- Direct: Redwood maintains entitlement records and can provide flexible seat management, transfers, and custom licensing terms.

5) Co-sell & incentives
- Marketplace: listing on AWS/Azure/GCP can enable co-sell motions and cloud seller incentives, channel credits, and joint GTM. However, co-sell support often requires formal partner registration and additional paperwork (partner agreements, partner references).
- Direct: co-sell is possible via partner programs but marketplace listing often provides more direct route for cloud sales teams to participate.

6) Compliance / evidence
- Marketplace vs direct: the underlying product is the same—SOC2, encryption, audit logs are available regardless of procurement route. However, some marketplaces surface additional attestation docs; private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and specific compliance packs often require separate contracts or addenda.

7) Termination & data portability
- Marketplace: termination flow depends on provider billing cycles; we still provide standard data export (logs, snapshots, KV prefix) per our data retention policy.
- Direct: easier to negotiate retention windows, egress assistance, and exit support SLAs.

Recommended initial path for Acme:
- If speed-to-value is top priority and procurement wants minimal legal negotiation: pursue a standard marketplace transactable listing (AWS or Azure) and a private offer if you need negotiated pricing.
- If you need custom commercial terms, multi-year commitments, or specific SLAs/SOWs (Dedicated or Private deployment) — go direct.

Next steps: I attached a one-pager that summarizes the tradeoffs and a checklist for which procurement route makes sense. Would be happy to join procurement call — proposed slots Tue 4/13 10–11am or Wed 4/14 2–3pm PT.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[aisha_rahman@redwood.ai]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, Apr 11, 2026 at 08:30 AM -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace vs direct purchase — procurement questions

Folks — forwarding Acme’s procurement questions and my response. Quick internal notes / ask:

- Acme is leaning toward marketplace for speed, but they flagged the need for a private offer if they want a discount and net45 terms. They asked about co-sell incentives — looks like they want the cloud incentives to offset some of the marketplace fees.
- For Azure private offer we can do partner-managed private offers; for AWS we can offer an AWS Marketplace Private SaaS Offer (requires some onboarding). Both enable negotiated pricing while keeping provider billing. GCP has a similar private pricing flow but is less commonly used by this account.
- Legal: if we go private offer route we need to confirm whether the partner fee/marketplace fee constrains our ability to give back-end discounts. Marcus — can you confirm margin impact and whether we can absorb 3rd-party fees for a top-line discount?
- Rachel — if we pursue private offer + co-sell, can you enumerate required partner enrollment steps and the expected timeline for partner approval? I think procurement will push for net45 and an invoice flow that passes through Acme’s cloud reseller.

Also: recommend we prepare a concise SOW addendum that covers Dedicated/Private deployment options (if Acme needs data residency or an on-prem package). If they go marketplace transactable now, we can pilot on hosted Redwood and contract for Dedicated later.

Attn: keep language tight in any marketplace private offer so it doesn't inadvertently change our SLAs — we should prefer to keep SLAs in our own MSA where practical.

Thanks —
Aisha

Hi Julia / Acme procurement,

Following up with a consolidated answer and concrete next steps. Summary attached and a short workbook with suggested routes based on your priorities.

Decisions / recommended path based on your priorities:
- If speed and minimal legal review wins: start with a standard marketplace listing on the cloud provider you prefer (AWS or Azure). This gets you transactable quickly; we can provide SOC2 artifacts and standard data export tools immediately.
- If you require negotiated pricing, net45, or specific deployment (Dedicated / Private with data residency): proceed with a Private Offer (marketplace-managed private offer) or direct contract. Private Offers give you negotiated price + cloud billing; direct gives the most flexibility on terms and invoicing.

Concrete next steps:
1) We’ll prepare an Azure private offer and an AWS Private SaaS Offer draft to show the pricing delta vs list.
2) Marcus will confirm discount capacity and whether Redwood will absorb marketplace fees for the proposal.
3) Rachel will list partner enrollment steps and expected calendar for co-sell enablement.
4) Schedule a 30-min procurement review — proposed Wed 4/14 2:00pm PT. Please confirm.
